desc: The second executive action of 2026 and the one that goes to witnesses rather than paper. In July 2026 the administration directed the Department of War and the intelligence community to waive nondisclosure agreements for former government employees and contractors wishing to share UAP information with authorised investigators. Senior officials described the mechanism as abrogation of prior NDAs for people cooperating through proper channels, executed by having former officials meet cleared officials of AARO or a presidential PURSUE task force who may waive the applicable NDAs during authorised discussions, with any resulting information routed through existing declassification procedures. Officials were explicit that this is not a declassification directive: it permits disclosure to government investigators, not to the public. Rep. Eric Burlison, whose Special Advisor is David Grusch, said on 29 July 2026 that he had been calling for exactly this, offered his office as a channel, and recommended that anyone participating request congressional presence alongside legal counsel. That recommendation is the whole lesson of the Grusch episode compressed into a sentence: the last person to route a disclosure exclusively through executive-branch channels lost his clearance, his promotion and his career while his identity left the protected channel.
